findings.title: The only focus indicator is a 1px dashed underline, which is below the minimum focus appearance
findings.detail: WCAG 2.2's Focus Appearance (2.4.11, AA) requires the focus indicator to cover at least the area of a 2px-thick perimeter of the control and to have at least 3:1 contrast against the unfocused state. A 1px dashed text underline meets neither, and it does nothing at all for controls with no text — icon buttons, the carousel arrows, the map controls. Compounding it, Quasar's own focus affordance is explicitly disabled (`.q-focus-helper { display: none }`) and `outline: 0` is set on every focusable Quasar element.
evidence: Sole focus rule in the production stylesheet: :focus-visible{ text-decoration: underline 1px dashed; }
.q-focus-helper { display: none } — Quasar focus ring suppressed

findings.title: Checkout imposes a ~15-minute time limit with no way to turn it off, adjust it, or extend it
findings.detail: WCAG 2.2.1 (Level A) allows a time limit only if the user can turn it off, adjust it to at least ten times the default, or extend it with a simple action after a warning. This checkout offers none of the three. The limit spans a four-step form that asks for guest names, an organisation, a team, payment details and policy acknowledgements — a user relying on a screen reader, a switch device, voice control, or simply reading carefully can very plausibly exceed it and lose the reservation. This is the single highest-severity finding in the audit: it can make the booking flow impossible to complete rather than merely difficult.
evidence: Countdown found in production markup, starting at 14:52
No extend, pause, or disable control present in the DOM
